item.title: Price beats Kotaskova to become undisputed champion
item.description: Lauren Price hopes to fight on bigger stages as her career continues [Getty Images] Lauren Price dominated Michaela Kotaskova to seal her place in history by becoming undisputed world welterweight champion. Price, 32, took an unanimous, shut-out decision and the acclaim of the crowd to add the WBO title to her collection and become the first Welsh fighter to claim the accolade of holding all four major world titles. Already an Olympic champion and world champion from her amateur days, it further underlined her claim as being among the very best in boxing. But the way in which she did it, extending a perfect professional record to 11 wins from her 11 fights, suggested there could yet be more to come. Price v Kotaskova: Watch undisputed title fight after Edwards v McGregor History, hunger and headline bills - why Price is box office Edwards' world title aim to join Welsh boxing greats Price won every round from every judge in front of a partisan Cardiff crowd, producing an unrelenting pace that punished her opponent at every opportunity. Although Price could not force a stoppage, there was never any doubt she had done enough against an opponent full of stamina and stubbornness. Kotaskova, beaten only once, but never stopped in her career, showed real heart but had no answer to Price's expertise. The Tokyo gold medal winner could celebrate even before the final bell sounded, climbing the corner ropes and into the record books. It was lapped up by a sell-out Utilita Arena crowd who excitedly acknowledged the achievement and the moment. Wales has produced 14 world champions, some of them genuine greats. They include, of course, Joe Calzaghe who so often graced this venue with successful defence after successful defence of his super-middleweight crown. He never reached undisputed status, though he was able to cross the capital city to go from arena to stadium champion. That is the next challenge for Price, claiming before she left the ring that more is to come while talk immediately turned to five-weight world champion Claressa Shields as a stadium fight next summer. Champions recognise champions That is for the future, but this was a night for history - with the calibre of some of the former boxers in the stands a nod to that. Champions know champions. Five Welsh world title winners were in the capital to watch their compatriot do something never been done before. From Cinderella Man Steve Robinson and Barry Jones, to the more recent Joe Cordina, who may still be eyeing a stadium return of his own in the coming weeks. All have been proud to fly the flag, but perhaps none have worn it quite as much on their sleeve - or shorts - as Price has done. item.title: Newport not taking anything for granted - Mullins
item.description: [Huw Evans Picture Agency] On this day a year ago, Christian Fuchs was appointed Newport County head coach , but now under another former Premier League player, Newport continue to make significant strides forwards – albeit with a much stronger and experienced squad. Newport County's progress under Hayden Mullins has been clear to see, but the Exiles boss was keen to stress that his side will not get carried away. County welcome Swindon Town to Rodney Parade on Saturday, 21 November (12:30 GMT) looking to extend their unbeaten home league record, having already collected 15 points on home soil, just seven shy of the 22 County managed across the entirety of the last campaign. While their away form remains a work in progress, Newport continue to climb the League Two table and earned a credible point at play-off hopefuls Crewe Alexandra last weekend despite leading 2-0. "The boys have done really well," said Mullins. "They have gone into games where people would have given us no chance [and picked up points]. "No one would have said we'd be 2-0 up at half-time on Saturday and potentially could have won the game, so it was a good performance to come out with a draw away from home. "We've been really unlucky not to pick up the results I felt we've deserved. In certain moments in games our performances have let us down and we need to address that to give us the opportunity to be a little bit higher." Having already beaten Swindon 2-0 in the EFL Trophy this season confidence within the squad is growing, but Mullins insists Newport must remain focused. "We're not taking anything for granted," he added. "We want to work hard, take every game as it comes, not look past any games and make sure we're set up in the right way for every game." That mindset is shared by defender Dan Sassi, who, though Newport have just one win in their last five league games feels Newport should not fear anybody. "We fancy ourselves against anyone in this league," said Sassi. "We've got some great talent in the group and the spirit is amazing. We're taking it game by game, but we're definitely looking upwards." For a club that spent much of last season looking over its shoulder, that growing sense of looking upwards is perhaps just the relief they craved.

item.description: Four weeks ago, Rutgers took a set off Michigan State at Jersey Mike’s Arena, 28-26, in a four-set loss that at least had an argument in it. In the first Big Ten Tournament match in program history, they did not reach 17 points in any of three sets. Michigan State swept Rutgers 25-16, 25-15, 25-13 on Friday at Fishers Event Center in Fishers, Ind., in the first round of the inaugural Big Ten Tournament, a match that was over in 81 minutes in front of an announced 6,866. The No. 11 seed Spartans move on to No. 6 Minnesota on Saturday. The No. 14 seed Scarlet Knights go home, and the season is over. Michigan State hit .415 with 48 kills and nine attack errors on 94 swings. Rutgers hit .065 with 25 kills and 19 errors on 92. Rutgers’ best set was the one they hit .129 in, and they lost that one 25-13. The worst part is that Rutgers was level or ahead in all three sets, at 5-5 in the first, 11-9 in the second and 6-4 in the third. From those three scores to the end of each set, Michigan State outscored them 57-22. That is about as bad as an 11-versus-14 matchup gets. item.title: How Does Royce Lewis Fit On Dodgers After Reported Trade?
item.description: Minnesota Twins first baseman Royce Lewis The Los Angeles Dodgers have reportedly acquired Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins in exchange for Bobby Miller and Francisco Espinoza, according to FanSided's Robert Murray . Lewis was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2017 MLB Draft and looked like a star in the making after he made his debut in 2022. However, he has failed to live up to high expectations and has been held back by countless injuries. Miller was once the No. 2 prospect in the Dodgers organization, so it's essentially a trade of great prospects who may need a change of scenery after failing to live up to the hype. Lewis is a versatile defender and could be used in a utility role. The Dodgers are pretty much set when it comes to starters, but Lewis could fill the void left by Miguel Rojas retiring. The Dodgers have aging veterans Mookie Betts, Max Muncy and Freddie Freeman who may need more days off moving forward. Lewis can play all of their positions, and the hope is that the Dodgers can unlock his full potential on offense. Lewis had a .307/.364/.549 slash line with 17 home runs in his first 70 games as a big leaguer. Since then, he does have 44 home runs, but an overall OPS of .689. There is pop in his bat, but he strikes out a ton. He is kind of an all-or-nothing type of hitter right now, but that could change with the proper coaching. He was a non-tender candidate, but the Dodgers clearly liked him enough to trade for him. More MLB: Reds Slugger Wins 2026 NL Rookie Of The Year

item.title: Diamondbacks non-tender Andrew Saalfrank and Blake Walston
item.description: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 05: Relief pitcher Andrew Saalfrank #27 of the Arizona Diamondbacks pitches against the Boston Red Sox during the eighth inning at Chase Field on September 05, 2025 in Phoenix, Arizona. The Diamondbacks defeated the Red Sox 10-5. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today was the the deadline for teams to decide on whether or not to offer contracts to the players in their arbitration seasons and below. The D-backs did so for just about everyone on their list, but there were a couple of notable exceptions. Of the players on the Arizona roster eligible for arbitration, they made the (largely no brainer) decisions to extend contracts to all three: C Gabriel Moreno, RHP Ryne Nelson and OF Lars Nootbaar. However, two other pre-arbitration players, both left-handed pitchers – Andrew Saalfrank and Blake Walston were non-tendered, and so have now become free agents. Saalfrank is perhaps the better known of the pair, for reasons both good and bad. The then 26-year-old exploded onto the team late in the 2023 season, not allowing an earned run in his first ten appearances in the major-leagues. That got him a spot on the D-backs post-season roster that year, and he added four more scoreless outings in the Wild Card and Divisional Series, before giving up a run Game 3 + 4 of the NLCS. He got a blown save in the former, although the D-backs won. He finished the playoffs with a 3.18 ERA across 11 post-season games, and was expected to be a big part of the Arizona bullpen for 2024. He didn’t make the Opening Day roster and, after being called up in April, a disastrous outing in Los Angeles got him quickly optioned back to Reno. Worse was to come: in June, word came that he had been found guilty of gambling on baseball. There’s no indication he ever bet on himself, and he was by all accounts quite terrible. But a year’s suspension was mandatory, derailing him entirely. Saalfrank returned the following year, and pitched very well down the stretch (a 1.24 ERA across 29 innings). But this February he had shoulder surgery to remove bone spurs and perform a labrum repair. He never made it back to the mound and it appears his time with the team is now over. Walston only made nine appearances at the major-league level, the first coming back in May 2024. However, he had Tommy John surgery in early 2025, which cost him the entire season and then some. He only returned to the minor-leagues in August this year. Though Blake did get a cup of coffee in September with the big-league club, allowing a run over three innings. But, again, it seems the D-backs had no further use for him. With both players being pre-arbitration, their departures won’t move the needle much with regard to payroll. item.title: Giants ink former All-Star closer to $6.3 million contract
item.description: The San Francisco Giants are coming off a dreadful 2026 season. There were holes throughout the roster, but one that might have been shored up to some degree on Friday with the news that the Giants came to terms with relief pitcher Camilo Doval on a one-year, $6.3 million contract, per The Athletic. Doval’s journey brought him back to the San Francisco Giants late in 2026 and he’ll remain there for at least 2027. The 29-year-old right-hander was claimed by the Giants off waivers from the Pittsburgh Pirates in late September after San Francisco traded him to the New York Yankees ahead of the trade deadline in 2025. Camilo Doval throws a pitch for the New York Yankees during a game against the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park on Wednesday, March 25, 2026. Charles Wenzelberg/New York Post It was a full circle moment for Doval, who signed with the Giants as an amateur free agent in 2015 as an 18-year-old. He made the All-Star team once in 2023 when he led MLB with 39 saves while striking out 87 hitters in 67 2/3 innings. Next season would be his seventh with the team. The Yankees acquired Doval to bolster their bullpen by sending four prospects back to the Giants in 2025. Doval appeared in 22 regular season games and three playoffs contests for New York, who lost in the Divisional Series to the Toronto Blue Jays in four games. San Francisco Giants pitcher Camilo Doval (75) pitches against the Miami Marlins in the ninth inning at Oracle Park in San Francisco on Friday, April 8, 2022. USA TODAY Sports The Giants initially traded Doval during a strong season in 2025 when he had a 3.09 ERA in 47 games. His ERA jumped to 4.82 over the remainder of the season with New York, who traded him to Pittsburgh for a pair of prospects Aug. 1. item.title: Capitalizing on motion and play-action inside the Jaguars offense
item.description: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 15: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars hands the ball to Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the first half of the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) Johnnie Izquierdo The Jaguars’ offense has been exceptional this season. That’s not really a secret. Seemingly anything and everything Liam Coen implements strikes gold. Among those things is the Jaguars’ success with motion, play under-center, and with play-action. In 2026, Trevor Lawrence is seeing career-highs in use of motion (75.2%), play under-center (45.7%), and play-action (26.8%). The Jaguars just so happen to be about the best team in the NFL in all three departments. Jacksonville’s use of motion over the years is a confusing one. Former head coach Doug Pederson stayed pretty consistent in his use of motion, despite the league seeing a dramatic uptick. In 2024, his final season in Jacksonville, the Jaguars ranked 31st at just 47.9%. Since then, Liam Coen has nearly doubled that figure in two seasons. The Jags are now seeing pre-snap motion on 75% of snaps, the fourth-highest mark in the league. As a whole, the team ranks third in yards per game (281.3), third in yards per play (6.2), and second in EPA per play with motion. It’s no surprise then to see Lawrence has the second-most passing yards in the league with 1,613 yards. On the ground, the Jags rank sixth in yards (873) when utilizing motion. From under-center, Trevor Lawrence is completing 73.3% of his passes for 665 yards, six touchdowns, zero interceptions, and an NFL-best 142.7 passer rating. His 11.08 yards per attempt, 73.3% completion rate, 63.3% success rate, and +0.59 EPA per play all rank either first or second in the NFL. The Jags’ ability to run the ball from under-center certainly helps the cause. Bhayshul Tuten ranks fifth in the NFL with 509 yards gained from under-center, according to Fantasy Points. It’s that success that makes the Jaguars’ use of play-action so deadly, a new tool at Trevor Lawrence’s disposal. When using play-action, Lawrence has completed 72% of his passes for 797 yards, six touchdowns and zero interceptions, and another NFL-best passer rating of 133.0. He again is Top-2 in yards per attempt (10.6), success rate (64%), and EPA per play (+0.552). It’s this marriage of coaching and talent between Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence that has made this Jaguars’ offense so scary. Yes, Trevor Lawrence is playing the best football of his career and maybe in the entire NFL. item.title: Dustin May’s Four Rings Prove Baseball’s New Reality
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Dustin May (21) pitches during the first inning against the Tampa Bay Rays during Game 4 of the World Series at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. on Oct 27, 2026. Dustin May has four World Series rings, and that number is now shared only with Mookie Betts among active players. The former Dodgers pitcher reached this milestone after helping the Milwaukee Brewers eliminate Los Angeles in the 2026 National League Championship Series. “It’s crazy to fathom that I have four rings,” May said. “It’s kind of something that not many people in this world have ever accomplished and it’s crazy to even think that my name is attached to that.” The Road Was Not Smooth May’s path to the fourth ring was filled with physical pain and unexpected twists. He sat out the full 2024 campaign while healing a torn flexor tendon located in his right arm. An esophageal tear resulting from a freak accident involving a salad required surgery, making things worse. Despite missing time, he still earned a championship ring for the 2024 campaign. Once he resumed playing as a workhorse for the Dodgers during 2025, the Boston Red Sox acquired him at the deadline. He was credited with another ring that season despite leaving the team early. Money Follows The Wins A winning performance with Milwaukee during the second half of the 2026 season probably increased his market value this winter. After securing a three-year, $52.5 million contract in free agency, May now is a pitcher for the Chicago White Sox. This contract shows that teams still pay big for proven winners, even when their recent history includes major injuries. The Cost Of The Spotlight While May celebrates, other players struggle with the pressure that comes with winning and losing. Walker Kessler, who plays for the Los Angeles Lakers, recently discussed how scrutiny can ruin the joy of sports. He noted that some players enter the league loving the game but get blinded by the extra noise. “So they lose the love of the game because they focus so much on all the other stuff, and it’s sad to see,” Kessler said on The Old Man and the Three podcast. May seems to have avoided that trap, keeping his focus on the work rather than the noise. His four rings stand as proof that the game can still be enjoyed if the player stays true to the grind.

(Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Michael Reaves/Getty Images NAPLES, Fla. — A Lim Kim pulled away from a crowded pack in a most spectacular fashion Friday when she made a hole-in-one on the par-3 16th hole and posted an 8-under 64 to build a three-shot lead over defending champion Jeeno Thitikul in the CME Group Tour Championship. It also helped that Kim picked up birdies on all four of the par 5s at Tiburon Golf Club. She finished with a long two-putt par to reach 15-under 129, the lowest 36-hole score since this tournament moved to Tiburon in 2013. Nelly Korda, in her bid to win the season finale to get into the LPGA Hall of Fame, shot a 67 and still wound up losing ground. She started three shots behind and now is six back on a course that has been relatively soft with wide fairways that allow for low scoring. She hit 7-iron from 168 yards that pitched in front of the pin, took one bounced and disappeared. She stretched out both arms in a quiet, surprised celebration. Kim followed with a 5-foot birdie on the par-5 17th and is halfway home to $4 million prize, the richest payoff in women’s golf. “I needed 155-yard shot, honestly a little strong hit and I make it,” Kim said of her ace. “A little luck to me, yeah.” She still has a solid chasing pack behind her. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
